runtime.execution: Synchronous multi-step generators, provider adapters, local AST interpreter state, threaded tool calls and optional remote Jupyter executors.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns Python agent memory/state and default local or created remote executor; consumes model/tool/MCP dependencies. Docker executor creates/cleans its kernel/container, rather than leasing an existing shared kernel.

summary: Python code is a native agent action combining tools, managed agents and arbitrary authorized computation across retained executor variables.

inspection.scope: MultiStepAgent run/finalize, CodeAgent/tool dispatch, local timeout/state, Docker kernel ownership, memory/export and source oracles
inspection.limits: No downloaded code/tests run; no full provider/MCP or isolation conformance assessment. AST restrictions are not treated as a security sandbox.

actions.name: run / interrupt
actions.output: final answer or RunResult, streamed steps
actions.lifecycle: interrupt between steps; reset chat/monitor but preserves executor state

actions.name: python_interpreter / final_answer
actions.input: parsed Python program with tool/agent calls and state variables
actions.lifecycle: stateful per executor; logs/output capped; no atomic state rollback on failure
actions.authority: authorized imports/functions/tools; local AST interpreter not security sandbox

actions.name: execute_tool_call / process_tool_calls
actions.output: typed native value/observation/error; media stored in agent state
actions.lifecycle: parallel future completion; retained order ID-sorted
actions.authority: known tools/agents, argument validation/sanitize native I/O

actions.name: managed_agent.__call__
actions.output: rendered report plus optional truncated summary
actions.lifecycle: synchronous agent run; separate model permitted; remote executor disallows
actions.authority: configured registered agent name, no peer room protocol

actions.name: LocalPythonExecutor.send_variables / send_tools / __call__
actions.lifecycle: resident state survives calls until object destroyed; timeout not hard kill
actions.authority: host functions/import whitelist configurable including broad authority

actions.name: DockerExecutor.run_code_raise_errors / cleanup
actions.lifecycle: creates own kernel, per-call websocket; cleanup stop/remove
actions.authority: operator config/host Docker authority; not shared-kernel consumer lease

actions.name: step_callbacks / final_answer_checks / get_full_steps / save
actions.input: callback/check functions, agent state or output directory
actions.output: mutations/check verdicts, step dicts, agent/tool code/config artifacts
actions.lifecycle: finalize each step, checks before finish; export ignores callbacks/checks, no heap checkpoint
actions.authority: operator-supplied host callbacks and final policy

filesystem.detail: Authorized imports/local tool callables can expose host filesystem; remote code uses created container kernel. No default general coding filesystem tool inferred.

processes.detail: Authorized host functions/imports or remote kernel can start programs; only executor container ownership/cleanup traced, no native durable child registry.

code_actions.detail: Native CodeAgent python_interpreter action parses Python and composes tool/managed-agent calls, variables and final_answer; JSON tool agent separate.

persistent_kernel.detail: AST state persists across steps and conversation reset does not clear executor state; created remote Jupyter kernel persists until cleanup. No restart/shared multi-consumer lease or heap restore.

standing_database.detail: Resident memory/variables and pluggable tools can access DB; no general standing database supplied by these paths.

workflow_programming.detail: Model Python code programs control flow and tools/managed agents; per-step callbacks and optional planning/retry/final-answer checks program the agent.

multi_model.detail: Managed agent objects can use separate models and are callable as tools; remote-code path excludes managed agents.

live_collaboration.detail: Managed-agent task/report is synchronous delegation, with bounded report summaries; selected implementation no peer mail/room steering. Remote-code delegation explicitly restricted.

concurrent_work.detail: JSON tools/managed calls ThreadPoolExecutor runs independent calls, completion-order yields; no transaction settlement across external effects.

steering_interrupt.detail: Interrupt switch checked between steps; timeout future cannot kill running Python thread and executor context waits shutdown. Tests do not prove deadline return or external effect stop.

turn_redefinition.detail: Step callbacks receive mutable agent at finalize; planning/check policies and Python model actions configurable. No before-provider transform/hot turn-definition protocol traced.

compaction.detail: summary_mode projects messages omitting model/planning content and managed reports truncate; not managed compaction event with archived context lineage.

context_repair.detail: Mutable memory full steps and callbacks can reconstruct/change model context; reset clears stored steps and no corruption-repair protocol.

original_audit.detail: ActionStep includes model inputs/outputs/code and full-step export, but logs/output already truncated and reset deletes memory; model_output may be augmented closing tag, not untouched raw response.

audit_query.detail: get_full_steps/get_succinct_steps and replay/return_full_code expose structured per-run inspection; not persistent everything-query DB.

hot_change.detail: Python tool/agent dictionaries and finalize callback supply ordinary mutable machinery; executor tools sent at each run. No atomic live deployment/reload protocol established.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Save/from_dict exports agent code/configuration; callbacks/checks explicitly ignored and resident memory/executor heap omitted. No outpost refit/active work drain.

remote_services.detail: Remote executor choices and provider/native tool objects consume services; Docker/Jupyter lifecycle is agent-owned here.

self_improvement.detail: Code actions/callbacks/checks/export are ingredients for experiments, not a wired candidate harness evaluation/adoption loop.

complaints.detail: AgentError plus code/input/output/timing/step IDs provide diagnostics; no standing complaint table/state snapshot filing.

authority.detail: Allowed tools/imports/functions and argument validation; local executor explicitly not security sandbox, remote executor restrictions different. No routine approval pipeline seen in native code path.

evaluation.detail: Final-answer checks can inspect memory/agent state and force retry; timeout/AST/reset tests actual numerical/error/step assertions but no semantic validity of arbitrary check.

time_order.detail: Step timings/numbers and tool IDs; threaded effects execute completion order while persisted observations sorted IDs; no durable effect ordering/settlement.

evidence.claim: Run retains state/additional args and passes tools/variables to executor; reset clears conversation/monitor, not local executor state.
Step loop checks interrupt only before step, optional planner; error/finalize callback then append; final-answer callbacks assert and agent retries on failure.
CodeAgent records model input/output, parses/fixes code action, invokes python_interpreter, records logs and truncated output observation.
JSON tools including managed agents execute in thread pool; futures yield completion order then retained calls/observations sorted by ID.
Tool-name validation, state-reference argument substitution, validation and sanitized native or managed-agent call; errors converted into agent execution diagnostics.
Local executor keeps state/custom tools/import permissions across calls, explicitly not security sandbox, configured print cap and timeout.
AST operations mutate live state; print capture truncated before return/errors; timeout wrapper around execution without transactional rollback.

Timeout uses future.result inside ThreadPoolExecutor context; running thread cannot be force-killed. Context manager exit waits worker by ordinary executor semantics, so timeout exception alone does not establish prompt hard stop.
Executor selectable local/blaxel/e2b/modal/docker; cleanup called; managed agents explicitly unsupported with remote code execution.
Docker executor builds/starts own container, new authenticated Jupyter kernel and websocket calls; cleanup stops/removes container.
ActionStep stores inputs/output/code/tool calls/error/timing/state projection; serialization sanitizes values and images raw bytes, not universal transport/effect archive.
Memory is resident step list, reset deletes it; full/succinct exported steps and pretty replay are inspection, not replaying effects.
Managed agent renders task/report and optional bounded work summary; save exports tools/agent/prompts/UI/requirements code artifacts.
to_dict serializes configuration/tool code/provider configuration and ignores callbacks/final-answer checks; not live memory/kernel checkpoint.
Step callback registry accepts per-step class callbacks; caller receives agent at finalize for normal-operation mutation.
Timeout tests assert eventual error and completion/thread finished within generous bound, not deadline latency/no post-timeout side effects.

tests.focus: AST state/tool protection and threaded timeout mechanics
tests.oracle: Exact state/result/error tests plus timeout/thread join assertions. Timeout tests require eventual exception and thread completion, but do not measure prompt deadline nor prove killed worker/effects; source uses waiting executor context.

tests.focus: chat reset and final-answer validation retry
tests.oracle: Fake models produce exact number 7.2904, assert memory step counts 3/5/3 with reset, rejecting check diagnostics and accepted final step count. Does not prove reset clears interpreter variables or arbitrary answer correctness.

strengths: Code combines tool calls/control flow/variables natively instead of one JSON action per operation.
ActionStep retains rich request/code/result structure and checks/callbacks have actual agent access.
Interpreter and remote kernel boundaries visible and local non-sandbox claim explicit.
limits: Thread future timeout is not a kill boundary and context-manager shutdown may delay exception until worker completion; tests lack hard latency/effect oracle.
Conversation reset does not reset executor state; exported agent code/config does not checkpoint heap or callback policy.
Owned remote kernels/cleanup and managed-agent restrictions differ from shared fabric consumers.
arconaut_questions: How should logical turn reset, model-context reset and external computation-state reset be independent named operations?
Can code actions retain uncapped original output and exact source/generated transforms while offering bounded model views?
What executable refit barrier proves worker settlement beyond timeout exceptions?
